I’m sorry—I don’t have permission to pull real‑time product details straight off Amazon’s website. However, I can walk you through two common ways people gather that kind of information: | Method | What You Need | How It Works | |--------|---------------|--------------| | **Amazon Product Advertising API** | • An AWS account
• Access keys & secret tokens
• “Associate Tag” (you’ll receive one when you sign up)
• `boto3` library (Python SDK) | 1️⃣ Sign up at .
2️⃣ Create IAM users / generate access keys.
3️⃣ Install boto3 (`pip install boto3`).
4️⃣ Use the `get_items()` call specifying `"ItemIds": ["B09XYZ"]` where B09XYZ is the ASIN of the Galaxy S24. The JSON payload will contain `` and `` fields. | | **Web Scraping (with caution)** | • Python environment
• `requests`, `beautifulsoup4`, optionally `selenium` for dynamic pages
• Knowledge of HTML structure of Amazon product page | 1️⃣ Find the ASIN (e.g., `B09XYZ`) – usually part of the URL: `amazon.com/dp/B09XYZ`. 2️⃣ Build a request: ```python import requests from bs4 import BeautifulSoup ASIN = "B09XYZ" URL = f"https://www.amazon.com/dp/{ASIN}" HEADERS = { # Mimic a normal browser so Amazon doesn’t block us "User-Agent": ("Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64)" " AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko)" " Chrome/115.0 Safari/537.36"), } resp = requests.get(URL, headers=HEADERS) html = resp.text ``` 3️⃣ Parse out the price and shipping sections. For many products the price lives inside a tag with id `priceblock_ourprice` or similar; shipping often appears under a div with class `a-row a-spacing-mini`. Example extraction: ```python soup = BeautifulSoup(html, "lxml") def find_price(): ptag = soup.find(id="priceblock_dealprice") \ or soup.find(id="priceblock_saleprice") \ or soup.find(id="priceblock_ourprice") return ptag.get_text(strip=True) if ptag else None def find_shipping_policy(): ship_div = soup.select_one("div.a-row.a-spacing-mini span[data-a-color='secondary']") return ship_div.get_text(strip=True) if ship_div else None print(find_price()) print(find_shipping_policy()) ``` | ### Things To Keep In Mind * **Legal & Ethical:** Always respect Amazon’s Terms of Service. Heavy automated traffic may trigger CAPTCHAs or IP bans. * **Dynamic Content:** Some parts of the page load after JavaScript runs—if your simple `requests` script returns nothing useful, switch to Selenium or Playwright. * **Rate Limiting:** Add delays between requests (`time.sleep(2)`), rotate User‑Agents/IP addresses, or use proxies if you’re doing bulk work. * **Data Accuracy:** Prices fluctuate frequently; always timestamp your results. Shipping rules vary per region and seller, so double‑check whether the item ships free or has a fee. --- #### Quick Demo Using the Product Advertising API (Pseudo‑Code) If you already have valid credentials, here’s what the core logic looks like: ```python import boto3 client = boto3.client( "paapi5", aws_access_key_id="", aws_secret_access_key="" ) response = client.get_items( ItemIds=["B09XYZ"], Resources=[ "Offers.Listings.Price", # Current price "Offers.ShippingInfo.FreeShipping", "Offers.ShippingInfo.EstimatedDelivery.MinDays", "Offers.ShippingInfo.EstimatedDelivery.MaxDays" ], PartnerTag="", # Required even if you just want public data MarketplaceId="ATVPDKIKX0DER" # US marketplace ) item = response["ItemsResult"]["Items"][0] price_info = item["Offers"]["Listings"][0]["OfferListing"]["Price"] shipping_free = item["Offers"]["FreeShipping"] delivery_minmax = item["Offers"]["EstimatedDelivery"] print(f"Price: {price_info['DisplayAmount']}") print(f"Free Shipping: {'Yes' if shipping_free else 'No'}") print(f"Delivery window: {delivery_minmax['MinDays']}–{delivery_minmax['MaxDays']} days") ``` That gives you structured JSON back without having to parse raw HTML. --- Let me know if you’d like help setting up either method—or if there’s another platform/API you prefer!
